How the features are used in KITES
Two workflows built around the existing editor and processor views
KITES instruction scheduling and stall profiling
Suggestions workflow

1. Open or write code in Editor
2. Select a five-stage processor
3. Suggestions → Analyze
4. Inspect code moves and pipeline diagrams
5. Apply only after KITES verifies equivalent registers and data memory
Stall Profiler workflow

1. Run the program
2. Open Profiler
3. View costly lines and hazard causes
4. Use the heat gutter and cause table
5. Select Suggest fix when reordering may help
The profiler closes the loop: diagnose a stall, suggest a change, rerun, and compare.
Uniqueness and novelty
What this extension adds to the KITES simulator
KITES instruction scheduling and stall profiling
Source-level optimisation
The tool works from the user’s assembly code and can apply a verified reordering back into the editor.
KITES-aware model
The scheduler and profiler model the simulator’s forwarding and hazard behaviour rather than using generic timing assumptions.
Explainable output
Users see why an instruction moved, which stall it avoids, and a side-by-side pipeline trace.
Closed diagnostic loop
The profiler identifies expensive lines and links directly to a possible scheduling fix.

Key learnings and major challenges
Technical lessons from extending an existing simulator

Key learnings
Pipeline hazards, forwarding, cycle accounting, dependency DAGs, static scheduling, Qt/C++ integration, and test-driven debugging.
Development workflow
Using Claude Code and Codex skills to inspect a large codebase, implement features, test assumptions, and refine documentation.
Main challenge
The processor core, diagrams, profiler, and UI all depend on the same timing assumptions. A change in one layer needs validation in the others.
C++ growth area
The work strengthened practical C++ skills: project structure, classes, headers, build configuration, debugging, and tests.
Limitations
Clear boundaries of the current implementation
KITES instruction scheduling and stall profiling
Scheduling scope
Conservative, basic-block-only scheduling. Floating-point instructions and complex control flow act as barriers.
Processor model
The current simulator remains single-issue. The scheduler targets this timing model rather than superscalar execution.
These constraints keep every suggested reordering safe and explainable, but limit the optimisation opportunities.
Possible improvements
Natural extensions of the current scheduler and profiler
KITES instruction scheduling and stall profiling
Loop unrolling
Duplicate suitable loop bodies, then reuse the existing DAG scheduler to expose more independent instructions and hide more stalls.
Broader pipelines
Explore deeper stage counts, different forwarding paths, or an in-order two-lane pipeline model.
Cache modelling
Add cache-miss penalties to connect source-level choices with memory-system stalls.
Branch effects
Include branch-prediction behaviour in the same performance view.
